answer: Sybil resistance arises because each identity must post bonded collateral, while correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), rather than independent linear fines. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm, with asymmetric depreciation rapidly exhausting escrow value and making large coalitions uneconomical. Thus copper, hollow, and opal identities cannot cheaply mask shared control or dilute accountability.
